question: Why do heavily distorted rock guitars favour two-note power chords over full major chords?
answer: Because distortion invents notes: clipping adds tones at the sums and differences of the frequencies going in. A tempered fifth is almost exactly 3:2, so those new tones line up with the root's family. The tempered major third sits about 14 cents off a pure 5:4, so its products land off and beat: mud.
move: An ingredient that works alone can spoil once the heat is turned up.
reference: Esa Lilja, Dealing with the 3rd: Anatomy of distorted chords and subsequent compositional features in classic heavy metal, in Karjalainen & Kärki (eds), Modern Heavy Metal: Markets, Practices and Cultures, Aalto University, 2015, pp. 393–403
